fixes.explanation: Not quite. The LORD says, “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male.” (Exodus 13:2) What matters here is being born first, not holding the title of head of the house. Being first through the kitchen door doesn't make you the head baker, friend.

Goshen doesn't come up in these verses at all. Moses points the people back to a different day: the day they came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery (Exodus 13:3). That's the day to remember, not a night in Goshen. I bet it's a day nobody forgets.

Not this time. Moses says they'll keep this service once the LORD brings them into the land He swore to their fathers (Exodus 13:5). Goshen isn't named as the place for it. The service is tied to that promised land, the one flowing with milk and honey.

No priests are mentioned in these verses. Moses says, “…you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’” (Exodus 13:8) The explaining happens between the person speaking and his son. It's a close, personal kind of teaching, right on the day of the feast.

Doves don't come up in these verses. The donkey is redeemed with a lamb, and the verse adds that if it isn't redeemed, its neck is to be broken (Exodus 13:13). The verse also says every firstborn of their sons must be redeemed. So the lamb is for the donkey, and doves aren't part of it.

That's the answer, and it's a heavy one. Moses says, “…when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast.” (Exodus 13:15) Pharaoh was Egypt's king. That's why the Israelites sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but redeem all the firstborn of their sons.

That's what God says: “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.” (Exodus 13:17) The road went through the land of the Philistines, and it was shorter. God still didn't lead them that way. The reason has to do with what the people might do if they faced war.

Yes. “So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea.” (Exodus 13:18) God picked that road, not the shorter one through the Philistines' land. And the people followed where He led.

Moab doesn't show up here. The text says God led the people “…around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea.” (Exodus 13:18) Wilderness and the Red Sea are the direction it gives. North isn't mentioned at all.
That's right. “…the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.” (Exodus 13:18) They didn't walk out as a crowd with nothing ready. Arrayed for battle is exactly how the verse puts it.

The text says they were. “…the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.” (Exodus 13:18) So they left arrayed for battle, not a bunch of folks strolling out in their slippers. That's how the verse describes it.

That's it. “Moses took the bones of Joseph with him…” (Exodus 13:19) Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, “…you must carry my bones with you from this place.” So Moses carries them out of Egypt. That's a promise getting kept.

Right name, different item. The verse says Moses took “…the bones of Joseph with him…” and a coat isn't mentioned (Exodus 13:19). Bones is what the text names. Quite a thing to pack for a trip, friend.

Yes. “And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day…” (Exodus 13:21) By night He goes before them in a pillar of fire to give them light. Neither pillar left its place before the people (Exodus 13:22). Day or night, they could travel.
